title: Ops scrum spotcheck: UI rollouts & telemetry
content:
Quick morning spotcheck notes from the ops scrum (forced brief) - objective: validate there are no silent regressions in last night's UI rollout and sanity-check telemetry spikes we saw in staging/preview.

Attendees: Amira (owner), Daniel (telemetry), Riley (frontend), Sofia (rollouts), + ZD on call if needed

Summary:
- Canary A went healthy overnight. Canary B (10% exposure) shows 6.2% increase in JS error rate on embeddings route (panel/embeds) between 02:00-04:30 UTC. No correlated spike in backend 5xx.
- 95th percentile client render latency (panel list) moved from 420ms -> 980ms in EU region for a short 20-minute window at ~03:18 UTC.
- Spike appears tied to an experimental telemetry middleware (ld-ctx) introduced in PR 1892. Rolling back that middleware in staging removed the latency spike.
- No customer-facing incidents opened; feature flagged Canary B only. All users still within SLOs globally.

What we checked (playbook snippets):
- quick traces: tracer.search("panel.list", start="2027-08-11T02:45:00Z", end="2027-08-11T04:45:00Z") -> top op: sdk-telemetry->serialize (avg 240ms extra)
- kubectl: kubectl logs -n console canary-b-frontend -c web | grep "ld-ctx" | tail -n 200 -> shows repeated context serialization warnings
- influx query: SELECT percentile(latency,95) FROM client_render WHERE region='eu' AND route='panel.list' AND time > now() - 24h -> confirms 95p spike at 03:18

Initial hypothesis: the middleware (ld-ctx) serializes large cookie/prefetch-state blob for some users when feature flag A is on. This serialization path hits a pathological branch for a subset of sessions with big localStorage payloads from older clients. Result: CPU spike on the web worker thread and increased render latency.

Immediate actions taken during the scrum:
- Riley -> rolled back ld-ctx middleware flag for Canary B (FF: panel_ld_ctx) at 03:50 UTC. Observed latency return to baseline within ~8 minutes. (action recorded: CC-4321)
- Daniel -> created a tracing patch to sample and capture the offending payload for the next repro (link to trace snippet in CC-4321).
- Amira -> notified release leads and added note to the morning digest to watch EU latency this afternoon.

Follow-ups / Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Riley: add defensive size check to ld-ctx serializer + unit tests; open PR with feature gate to only run on modern clients (PR target: 1892 hotfix) — ETA EOD 2027-08-13. (linked: github PR draft)
- Daniel: add an alert threshold for client-side serialize time > 100ms aggregated over 5m (create alert in Grafana) — ETA 2027-08-12 morning. Jira: CC-4324.
- Sofia: update canary policy doc to include automated rollback if client-render 95p exceeds baseline by >50% for 15 minutes — ETA 2027-08-18. Confluence: Panel-Telemetry-Runbook (update stub).
- Amira: coordinate postmortem blameless notes and confirm rollback happened as intended; prep 1 pager for exec digest (if needed) — ETA 2027-08-13.

Low priority / Nice-to-have:
- Add pre-deploy static analyzer that flags large localStorage sync in client bundles (research: is there a lint we can run?) — backlogged for sprint-45.
- Run a synthetic job to fuzz-poke localStorage heavy sessions during canary to catch serialization regressions earlier.

Open questions we left in the meeting:
- How many customers actually hit the large payload path? (Daniel to produce histogram by customer id)
- Are older clients shipping a deprecated prefetch format that we need to migrate server-side? (PM sync recommended)
- Do we want automatic canary rollbacks or a staged manual hold? (ops posture discussion)

Notes to self / shortcuts captured: 
- Repro steps (dev): set localStorage.prefetch = JSON.stringify({big: new Array(120000).join('x')}); enable feature flag panel_ld_ctx for a test user; open /panel/list; watch devtools for main-thread long tasks.
- quick command to toggle FF (internal CLI): redwood-ff toggle panel_ld_ctx --canary=canary-b --off --auth-token $ADMINTOKEN

Meeting wrap:
- Short retro: communication flow worked (fast rollback), instrumentation gap: need better client-side serialize tracing pre-deploy.
- Decision: proceed with hotfix PR and add alerting; no wider rollback.
- Next check-in: 2027-08-12 09:30 UTC quick ops morning to confirm EU region stable.

Freeform notes:
- Riley: "We probably slipped a naive serializer in; shame on code review. I'll add explicit size guard rails."
- Daniel: "Tracing saved the day, make sampling config less conservative for client serialization traces."
- Sofia: "We should codify rollback windows and runbook owners per region; too much manual pinging last night."

Attached links (for handoff):
- Jira CC-4321 (incident doc, traces)
- PR 1892 (original middleware PR) 
- Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/console-rollouts/panel-telemetry?orgId=1

End of notes. Keep this doc as the quick ops artifact for the event; will convert to a short postmortem after follow-ups complete.
